title: Hershele and the Lost Face
summary: Rabbi Baruch of Mezhibozh sits in his room, sad and silent, and no one can make him laugh. Then — knock, knock! — in comes a little man with a lit candle in the middle of the day, searching under the table, in the soup pot and in an old boot. What is he looking for? The Rabbi's face, of course — everyone says it fell! A funny rhyming story about Hershele Ostropoler, the Hasidic jester, and a smile that came back home.
pages:
In Mezhibozh, Rabbi Baruch sat in his room,
sad and silent, his smile gone — lost in the gloom.
The Hasidim brought him tea, and cake on a tray,
but the Rabbi just sighed, "Oy..." like a worry cloud, gloomy and gray.

Then suddenly — knock, knock! The door opened wide,
and in came a little man with a lit candle — at noon! What a joke! — stepping inside.
His name was Hershele, and he lifted the candle high,
and looked under the table, and in the corner, and everywhere nearby.

"What are you looking for?" everyone asked. "What did somebody drop?"
"They told me the Rabbi's face fell! So I'm searching — all by myself, nonstop."
He crawled on the floor and cried: "I'm searching every place —
where is the Rabbi's face?"

He peeked into the pot — blub! Only noodle soup there.
He peeked into a boot — pee-yoo! Only socks... with a "lovely" smell in the air.
And all the Hasidim joined in, and Reb Tzvi too, in the chase:
"Where is the Rabbi's face?"

He climbed on a chair and peeked into the lamp up high,
then opened the window: "Goat! Have you seen it? Oh my!"
The goat poked its head in and bleated, "Meh-bbi? Meh-bbi?" all over the place:
"Where is the Rabbi's face?"

And the Rabbi watched, and watched, silent and still,
then suddenly — his beard trembled, and his mustache... gave a little laughing thrill!
Hershele leaped up with his candle: "Found it! It's here, right in its place!
Just a bit upside down... so hop! Let's flip over the Rabbi's face!"

And the Rabbi burst out laughing: Ha-ha! He laughed more and more,
he laughed till his beard wobbled, laughed and laughed like never before!
And the Hasidim laughed, and the cat laughed: Meow-ha!
And even the goat at the window: Meh-ha-ha-ha!

"Hershele," said the Rabbi, "sit here, right next to me, near,
and come tomorrow, and the day after, and every day — it's good to have you here!"
And from then on, every morning, Hershele came with a candle and a funny line,
and the Rabbi's room was filled with joy, and everything was fine.

One time Hershele came in — kling! klang! klong! —
with spoons peeking out of every pocket, and from his hat: ding-dong!
"Hershele," asked the Rabbi, "why all the spoons? What's wrong?"
"I've brought the Rabbi medicine — and not a bad one, it's good and strong!"

"The doctor said," whispered Hershele, "one spoon every half hour — that's what you do!"
And the Rabbi laughed: Ha-ha! — so loudly that out in the yard the goat heard it too.
In Mezhibozh, Rabbi Baruch sat in his room,
laughing and happy — his smile found, and gone was the gloom.
